Article Title: With nearly 40 mentions, ‘Mere pyare deshwasiyon’ dominates PM Modi’s Red Fort speech
Article Text:
With 10 mentions, 'Saathiyon' was the second-most use dphrase

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday addressed the nation from the ramparts of the iconic Red Fort in Delhi as the country celebrated its 80th Independence Day His 75-minute speech featured nearly 40 mentions of “Mere pyare deshwasiyon” (my beloved fellow citizens), making it the most-used phrase in his address.“Saathiyon” (friends) was the second-most used phrase, featuring 10 times in the speech.He also used “mere pyare yuva” (my beloved youth) once while calling on young people to join the fight against drugs and other addictions.The prime minister also used “desh sevak” (those who serve the nation) and “bhai beheno” (brothers and sisters) once each.Over the years, “deshwashiyon” (fellow citizens) has remained PM Modi’s go-to term for addressing the nation during his Independence Day speeches. He used the term 50 times last year, around 30 times in 2024, nearly 15 times in 2023 and more than 40 times in 2022. In 2023, however, his preferred form of address was “parivaarjan” (family member), which he used around 50 times.“Saathiyon” has also featured regularly in his Independence Day speeches. Modi used the term around 35 times in 2025, nearly 30 times in 2024, about five times in 2023 and approximately eight times in 2022.Meanwhile, the prime minister’s 2026 Independence Day speech was the fourth-shortest among his 13 consecutive August 15 addresses since his first in 2014. Saturday’s address was also his shortest in four years.His 2025 speech was his longest at 103 minutes, surpassing his previous record of 98 minutes in 2024. His shortest Independence Day address came in 2017, when he spoke for 56 minutes.PM Modi’s first Independence Day address in 2014 lasted 65 minutes. Since then, his speeches have ranged from under an hour to more than 100 minutes. He spoke for 88 minutes in 2015, 96 minutes in 2016, 83 minutes in 2018 and nearly 92 minutes in 2019.His address lasted 90 minutes in 2020, 88 minutes in 2021, 74 minutes in 2022 and 90 minutes in 2023.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the nation from the ramparts of the iconic Red Fort in Delhi. His 75-minute speech featured nearly 40 mentions of “Mere pyare deshwasiyon” (my beloved fellow citizens) “Saathiyon (friends) was the second-most used phrase, featuring 10 times in the speech.

Article Title: Narendra Modi becomes second PM to deliver 13th consecutive Independence Day speech
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi addresses the nation during the 8oth Independence Day celebrations, at Red Fort in New Delhi. (PTI image)

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday delivered his 13th consecutive Independence Day speech from the ramparts of the Red Fort, becoming the second prime minister after Jawaharlal Nehru to achieve the milestone.PM Modi has addressed the nation from the Red Fort every Independence Day since taking office in 2014. His latest address came on India's 80th Independence Day.Also read: 80th Independence Day - A throwback at PM Modi's signature Red Fort turbans Nehru, India's first prime minister, holds the record for the longest uninterrupted run of Independence Day addresses, having delivered 17 consecutive speeches from 1947 to 1963.PM Modi surpassed former prime minister Indira Gandhi, who delivered 11 consecutive Independence Day speeches between 1966 and 1976.PM Modi hoisted the National Flag at the Red Fort before beginning his address, with the ceremony synchronised with a 21-gun salute by the ceremonial battery.
Article Summary: PM Modi has addressed the nation from the Red Fort every Independence Day since taking office in 2014. His latest address came on India's 80th Independence Day. PM Modi surpassed former prime minister Indira Gandhi, who delivered 11 consecutive Independence Day speeches between 1966 and 1976.

Article Title: Justice Yashwant Varma cash-at-home row: Can Parliament still remove judge from office?
Article Text:
. Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings

NEW DELHI: There is little chance of the Lok Sabha continuing with Justice Varma’s removal motion despite the inquiry committee finding the charges relating to discovery of unaccounted currency notes in his official residential premises proved.As per Article 217(1) of the Constitution, a judge ceases to hold office if he/she resigns by sending a resignation letter written “under his hand addressed to the President”. Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings, finding the writing on the wall.How does a resignation of a constitutional court judge take effect? This question was answered by a five-judge bench of the SC in the Gopal Chandra Misra case on Feb 15, 1978. It was unanimous that once the judge sends his resignation to the President, he/she is deemed to have ceased to be a judge.In that case, the judge had set a prospective date for his resignation taking effect and before the arrival of the appointed date, he had withdrawn his resignation. SC had by four to one majority ruled that since the resignation was prospective, the judge had every right to withdraw it prior to the appointed date.
Article Summary: Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings. As per Article 217(1) of the Constitution, a judge ceases to hold office if he/she resigns by sending a resignation letter written “under his hand addressed to the President’

Article Title: Ready for long debate, can answer any question but opposition doesn’t want it: Amit Shah
Article Text:
Shah said govt had nothing to hide over an issue his rivals have used to attack him.

BJP

accuses Rahul of ‘anti-democracy, anarchic’ mindset

NEW DELHI: Home minister Amit Shah on Wednesday flung a challenge at the opposition for a comprehensive debate over police action during the anti-NEET protests in Delhi on July 20, saying he was ready for a 24-hour-long debate in Parliament at an hour’s notice over their charge of police excesses against protesting students. He said govt had nothing to hide over an issue his rivals have used to attack him.“If they give their consent for discussion to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla at 2 pm, a debate can begin at 3 pm and go on till 3 pm the next day. I am ready to answer any question. But they (opposition) do not want debate to take place in Parliament. Let the people decide who is running away,” he told the media a day before the end of the monsoon session, which has been marred by the opposition’s disruptions over a host of issues. Soon after, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said govt could even push for the session’s extension if the opposition wants.Shah said while the opposition had initially demanded his statement, govt had gone beyond it by agreeing to an extensive debate followed by his reply so that people could decide who was right and who was wrong.Amit Shah’s aggressive counter was seconded by a host of senior BJP functionaries, with party president Nitin Nabin saying the conduct of Rahul and the entire opposition was reflective of their “anarchic and anti-democracy” mindset.“The entire session is about to be over but they did not agree to a serious discussion over any issue,” he said, accusing them of running away after govt’s offer of a debate.With INDIA bloc MPs frequently accusing him of “running away” from Parliament, Shah hit back and said he was regularly in his chamber in the House. When the opposition was not letting the House function, what was the point of him going there, he asked.Expressing anguish at his opponents’ jibes like “lapata” (missing) and “bhagora” (fugitive) for him, Shah said these terms were being used only recently in parliamentary discourse.The minister later wrote to the Speaker, urging him to reach out to the opposition so that a discussion could begin. “You can allot as much time you think appropriate with mutual agreement. I want to participate in the discussion and I’m ready to answer every question of the opposition,” he said, adding that a solution to any issue in democracy emerged from dialogue and discussion.Congress had normalised disruption in Parliament, he said, adding a party which governed India for decades had fallen to such a low that it did not want discussion in the House.
Article Summary: Amit Shah said govt had nothing to hide over an issue his rivals have used to attack him. He said if they give their consent for discussion to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla at 2 pm, a debate can begin at 3 pm and go on till 3 pm the next day.

Article Title: Giant screens, screaming fans, Magnus Carlsen: Chess at EWC 2026 gets louder on the esports stage
Article Text:

TimesofIndia.com in PARIS:

(Image credit: Vineet Ramakrishnan/TimesofIndia.com)

India leaves Paris with two players in the top eight

(Image credit: Vineet Ramakrishnan/TimesofIndia.com)

Lucas had come to watch chess with his family. His wife was there, so was his young daughter and his 11-year-old son, Marius, who has been playing the game for only about a year.By the time they left the Esports World Cup arena at Paris Expo Porte de Versailles, Marius had something to take home - a signed autograph from Magnus Carlsen Around the chess stage were giant screens, music, commentary, noise-cancelling headphones and a crowd watching alongside the other Esports World Cup titles. “The screening, the show, the ambience. It's very nice,” Lucas said of the experience.Later on, Carlsen was back on that stage - this time with the trophy.The Norwegian defended his Esports World Cup Chess title, beating 19-year-old Denis Lazavik 2-0 in the grand final. Carlsen finished unbeaten and took home USD 250,000 and 1000 Club Championship points for Team Liquid. Lazavik earned USD 190,000 and 750 points.Hikaru Nakamura finished third with USD 145,000 after a chaotic third-place match against Alireza Firouzja, who finished fourth with USD 100,000.India's campaign ended with two players in the quarterfinals.Arjun Erigaisi and Nihal Sarin finished in the top eight and earned USD 72,500 each. Arjun was eliminated by Nakamura after their match went to Armageddon, while Nihal lost to Carlsen. M Pranesh finished ninth with USD 52,500, and Aravindh Chithambaram, who qualified through DreamHack Atlanta, walked away with USD 23,000.For the organisers, though, the five days in Paris were about more than finding another winner. Chess was being tested in a setting where 24 titles are being played across other tournaments - VALORANT, League of Legends, Dota 2, Rocket League, Fortnite to name a few.For Carlsen, there was no great need to decide whether chess had entered esports or esports had discovered chess.“I think regardless of the way you put it, I hope it can be a very happy marriage. That's what I will say. And I think this format really has been waiting for chess for a while,” the 35-year-old said in reply to a query from Timesofindia.com in a press conference post his title win.He went back much further than the EWC when explaining why.“You can see even as soon as people started having Internet in their homes, they started playing chess online. Like a lot of the best chess players migrated to not recently, but partly as online play as early as 1995. So it's certainly been coming, and I'm very happy that we're here where we present chess at a very good excited about it for that like this.”Carlsen had also made the point that what is being played here is not quite the chess that most people grew up watching.“I think this is just a little bit different, and I think we should embrace that. This is not kind of traditional chess, but this is jazz as an esport with all that brings, and I think we've done a really good job here the last two years of doing that with chess. So definitely hope to see more of that in the future, and I think it's serious,” he told reporters.The difference is not only in the format. There is the crowd, the stage, the noise around the players and the way the matches are presented. For someone who has spent much of his career playing in very different settings, this change has its own appeal for the Norwegian.“I think it's just in many ways better that you can have a little bit more, more of a fun experience. The way, the way it's going here. It's fast-paced and really demanding, but also fair for the players.”That was perhaps the interesting bit about watching the players here. Amid all the theatrics, the players themselves are still trying to do what they have always done - sit down and calculate the next move.Arkus Fredriksson has worked on making chess an esport for years. At a roundtable during chess week in Paris, he was less interested in explaining why chess belonged in the arena than in describing what it felt like to finally see it there.‘It's genuinely a dream come true’, said Fredriksson, adding, “We've wanted to be in arenas, screaming fans and all this, and it's taken a long time until we've finally kind of gotten here.”There had been earlier attempts. Fredriksson mentioned an event in San Francisco in 2016 and other experiments after that, but said they did not have the same production, scale, or quality as EWC.“Even just last year, it was the first time we brought commentary in the venue. With the noise-cancelling, that's something that we hadn't really done.”And then you can actually have people cheering and screaming, and we saw that last year and we're seeing that again this year, and I think more to come in the finals.”Morten Holst, Director of Games Partnerships at Esports Foundation, has a slightly different way of describing what the production is trying to do. He was not talking about changing the moves or the game itself. It was about giving viewers more to see.“It's not because we're trying to change what chess is about. We're not trying to invent digital chess, because the community already did that.”There is already a large online audience, he said.“They are growing up learning about chess, they are playing, they are watching, they are competing, and it's all happening digitally. They follow the streamers, the stars, they watch online tournaments, and they compete on platforms such as Chess.com.”That is where the EWC comes in. “And that's actually very similar to what you see across the board in many other games,” said Holst, citing the heart-rate monitor as one of the examples.“It's something that is so exciting that you normally see them being very calm, and they look like they are really handling stress well. So the heart-rate monitor shows you what the camera doesn't show.”And the players' presentation has changed too. A chess player would otherwise walk into a venue, usually in formal clothing, take a seat, and get on with the game. At EWC, the entrance itself has become part of the production.The fogger goes off. The music blares. The two players walk in from opposite sides and meet in the middle. Their faces appear on the giant screen behind them, the trophy sits between them, and they strike a face-off pose before taking their seats. The introductions are delivered at a pitch much closer to UFC’s Bruce Buffer than a traditional chess hall.It can feel theatrical. However, once the clocks start, the focus is still on the board with some added incentives for the live audience. They can see the players' reactions, their feet, their small movements, the moments when the pressure starts showing.“When we build out the stage, the desk they sit behind, you can see the feet, for example. So if they're tapping their feet or if they are doing other signs that they might be under pressure, we're really trying to get that out to the audience and get them closer to the audience,” adden Holst.Fredriksson sees another part of the change away from the board.“A lot of these players don't have big social media presences. They're not doing a lot of content on their own. They're very focused on the chess side.”Esports teams have now entered that space. “And now you have these esports teams with their existing fans and, you know, people are very curious about them, helping them create this content and build up their profiles and their presence.”He sees the movement going both ways. “So it is really, it's amazing, right? And it's bringing on all of these new kinds of fans to chess, which is great. And then vice versa, right? All these chess fans to these esports teams. And I think that's where this magic happens.”But, as much as technology is part of the attraction, there’s always a possibility of a hiccup. The third-place match between Nakamura and Firouzja was also a reminder that the technology is not foolproof.The two Team Falcons players were competing for third place when multiple disconnections disrupted the match. Nakamura was left waiting for around 20 minutes before officials told him the match would be recorded as a forfeit in his favour. Firouzja had left the arena.Nakamura initially believed Chess.com was responsible. He had no phone or outside information while waiting and said the first thing he saw on his screen was a disconnection.After being taken for interviews, he criticised Chess.com. He later retracted those comments. He subsequently learned that the issue had come from the EWC and had affected other events too.For an event trying to sell the idea of digital chess inside a physical esports environment, it was an uncomfortable interruption. The players were sitting in the same arena, but the game was still dependent on servers and connections working as they should.Despite that, the people behind the tournament remain bullish about chess' place in the EWC.Fabien Scheuermann, the Esports Foundation's Chief Games Officer, has been looking at the question from the other side - not why chess wants esports, but why esports wants chess.The Esports Foundation looks at viewership and attendance, an existing ecosystem for professional players, and cooperation with the platform or publisher when assessing games.“Chess is an absolute prime example of how to do it,” Scheuermann said at the roundtable.There is also a more practical reason for the EWC's involvement. More than prize money, for Scheuermann, the professionalisation of chess is as important as the arena spectacle.“Solo-player sports make it very, very difficult as a person or as a professional athlete to be profitable, right? You're running your own business. You are trying yourself to basically make sure that, as a professional athlete, make a profit and make a living out of this.”The club system gives players another route.“And through the Club Championship, we actually create this additional layer where chess players get picked up by professional organisations and get a salary, right? So you're not only competing for yourself and are not fully dependent on prize money, but actually with this you're increasing the stability, and someone else pays your salary, which also decreases your personal risk in going into this venture.”Fredriksson adds that more than 30 players were signed to esports teams after the first year of the EWC. Holst sees the EWC as part of a year-round digital chess calendar rather than something that should appear for five days and disappear again.“We hope that our events will create opportunities for other tournaments to start doing like you guys are doing. So there's opportunities all year long.”That is where the EWC's involvement starts becoming more interesting for players outside the very top of the game.Carlsen can win USD 250,000. A wider group of players could potentially earn a salary, have an esports organisation behind them, and compete throughout the year.The EWC is still only in its second year of chess. But that part of the experiment is already underway.In a hall built around gaming titles, chess had its own corner at the EWC 2026 - a board, two clocks, two players, giant screens and live audience - and a game that does not need much explaining once the pieces start moving.It came into a week of Counter-Strike 2, Rocket League, BGMI, and the rest of the EWC lineup without changing the game itself.At the end of it, Carlsen had the trophy, Arjun and Nihal had made the top eight, Nakamura had survived a technical controversy to finish third, and the young boy Marius had gone home with the autograph of the man who won it all. For chess, the pieces are beginning to settle into place in the world of esports.
Article Summary: Magnus Carlsen won the EWC chess title in Paris. The Norwegian beat Denis Lazavik 2-0 in the grand final. The five-day tournament was held at the Paris Expo Porte de Versailles. Chess was being tested in a setting where 24 titles are being played.

Article Title: Will Aaron Donald return to the Los Angeles Rams? Latest situation isn’t what fans hoped for as comeback decision looms
Article Text:
Will Aaron Donald return to the Los Angeles Rams? Latest situation isn’t what fans hoped for as comeback decision looms(Getty)

Sean McVay still has no final Aaron Donald answer for the Los Angeles Rams

Myles Garrett gives Aaron Donald another reason to return

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Aaron Donald still has not given the Los Angeles Rams a final answer about returning to the NFL. That remains the biggest piece missing from a comeback that once looked close to happening. The Rams have welcomed Donald back into their building, and the former defensive star has continued working out at a high level. However, Sean McVay’s latest comments suggest the team still needs to wait before expecting the three-time Defensive Player of the Year back on the field.The situation has changed from simple retirement speculation into a real possibility. Donald completed an official workout with the Rams, and McVay praised what he saw. Yet the workout did not settle the bigger question. Donald still needs to decide whether he wants to return after stepping away from football following the 2023 season.Sean McVay gave the clearest recent update on Saturday, and it was hardly the definitive answer Rams fans wanted. The coach said the organization remains in the process of working through the situation with Aaron Donald and does not want to put unnecessary pressure on him publicly.That approach fits McVay’s comments throughout the offseason. He has consistently made it clear that Donald controls the decision. The Rams can make the opportunity attractive, but they cannot decide whether the veteran wants to play another season.Donald has already shown that he can still move well enough to make the conversation serious. His official workout with the Rams gave the team another look at his physical condition after more than two seasons away from regular-season football. After watching the session, McVay said Donald looked great and described the workout as the “best tryout we’ve ever had.” He made those comments during his media availability after the workout.He said," He looked great. He's still continuing o go through the process. No new news on that front."Still, the Rams coach also made the important part clear. There was no new decision from Donald.That leaves Los Angeles in an unusual position. The team wants one of the greatest defensive players in franchise history back, Donald appears capable of competing again, and yet nobody can say when he will actually make his choice.The biggest attraction may be standing right next to Aaron Donald on the Rams' defensive line. Los Angeles acquired Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns this offseason, bringing the reigning Defensive Player of the Year into an already talented defense. The possibility of Garrett and Donald attacking quarterbacks together has naturally added fuel to the comeback story.Garrett has also acknowledged Donald’s interest in returning. The pairing could force offenses into difficult choices because both players have spent their careers commanding extra attention from offensive lines.Donald, however, has more to consider than the opportunity to chase another championship. He retired after 10 seasons with the Rams, finishing his career with 111 sacks, 10 Pro Bowl selections, eight first-team All-Pro honors and three Defensive Player of the Year awards.He also helped Los Angeles win Super Bowl LVI.Now the Rams have reached the point where the excitement needs to turn into a decision. Training camp has ended, the regular season is getting closer, and the team cannot plan around an unsigned comeback forever.For now, the door remains wide open. But until Aaron Donald makes the call himself, the Los Angeles Rams have no choice but to keep waiting.
Article Summary: Aaron Donald still has not given the Los Angeles Rams a final answer about returning to the NFL. Donald completed an official workout with the Rams, and McVay praised what he saw. Donald still needs to decide whether he wants to return after stepping away from football following the 2023 season.

Article Title: What happened to Jeremiyah Love? Latest injury update after Arizona Cardinals rookie’s preseason debut
Article Text:
What happened to Jeremiyah Love? Latest injury update after Arizona Cardinals rookie’s preseason debut(Getty)

Jeremiyah Love’s ankle injury keeps him out for the Cardinals’ next preseason game

Arizona Cardinals still have questions about Jeremiyah Love’s week 1 availability

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jeremiyah Love’s first preseason appearance gave the Arizona Cardinals plenty to feel good about, but it also ended with an ankle concern. The No. 3 overall pick impressed in Thursday’s 27-14 win over the Las Vegas Raiders before the Cardinals learned that he would need some time away from the field.The recent update arrived after head coach Mike LaFleur said Love felt more soreness than expected. Arizona will now keep its prized rookie out for the week and evaluate him again after he gets time to recover.Jeremiyah Love entered the Las Vegas Raiders game with plenty of attention on him after Arizona selected him third overall in the 2026 NFL Draft. The rookie quickly showed why the Cardinals made such a major investment in their new running back.On Thursday, Love handled 14 touches during the 27-14 victory. He carried the ball 11 times for 58 yards and added three receptions for 14 yards. His burst stood out throughout his limited action, and he even hurdled a defender during the performance.However, Love also picked up an ankle issue during the game. The Cardinals initially viewed the problem as minor. LaFleur even indicated after the game that Love could have returned if Arizona needed him.The situation looked slightly different when Love returned to the team on Friday, August 14. He experienced more soreness than the Cardinals expected, which led the coaching staff to change course and give him additional rest.LaFleur explained the decision while speaking with reporters on Saturday:“He came in yesterday a little bit more sore than he left,” LaFleur said. “We’ll keep him out this week as we just let it heal. It was a little more sore than we were anticipating.”That decision means Love will not practice this week and will miss Arizona’s preseason matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Saturday, August 22. The Cardinals plan to reassess his ankle after the week rather than rush him back onto the field.The bigger concern now involves the regular season rather than another preseason appearance. Arizona will open its 2026 campaign against the Los Angeles Chargers on September 13, giving Love several weeks to recover.Still, LaFleur has not promised that the rookie will return by Week 1. When reporters asked about a timetable, the Cardinals coach kept the focus on the immediate recovery process and said the team would reevaluate Love after this week.That makes the next medical update particularly important. The Cardinals have not announced a serious long-term diagnosis for Love, and current reports only indicate that he will miss at least this week because of the ankle soreness.Currently, Arizona appears to be choosing caution with its most valuable rookie running back. Love already showed his explosiveness against Las Vegas, so the Cardinals have little reason to push him through an ankle issue in the preseason. The next evaluation should provide a clearer idea of whether he can return before the Chargers game on September 13.
Article Summary: Jeremiyah Love made his Arizona Cardinals debut against the Las Vegas Raiders on Thursday. The No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft picked up an ankle injury in the 27-14 victory. Love will miss the Cardinals' next preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys.

Tom Brady’s unusual NFL broadcasting restrictions now have another name attached to them. Troy Aikman will face the same limits during the 2026 season after taking an advisory role with the Miami Dolphins. The NFL confirmed the decision of putting Aikman in a similar position to Brady as he prepares for another season in ESPN’s Monday Night Football booth.The move does not stop Troy Aikman from calling games for ESPN. Instead, it changes how much access he can have around NFL teams. That distinction matters because Aikman now has a relationship with one team while also working as a national broadcaster who covers the league.The NFL’s concern centers on information. Troy Aikman began working with the Dolphins in 2026 as a consultant during the team’s search for a new general manager and head coach. He remains an ESPN analyst while continuing his relationship with Miami. That combination creates the same type of information-access concern that followed Tom Brady after he became a minority owner of the Las Vegas Raiders while working for Fox.NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy confirmed the policy to Front Office Sports on August 14. He explained that the league would keep Brady’s existing parameters and apply them to Aikman as well.“There have been no issues with Tom over the last two seasons,” McCarthy said in a written statement to Front Office Sports. “The same parameters that pertained to Tom last season will continue this year and also will apply to Troy.”Those parameters are straightforward. Aikman can attend production meetings virtually, but he cannot attend practices or enter practice facilities. He can also interview players and football personnel away from team facilities, including at a team hotel in an area separated from other football staff.The league wants to keep a clear wall between Aikman’s Dolphins work and the information he receives as a broadcaster. That information can include team plans, player updates and other details that teams normally share with broadcasters during game preparation.Troy Aikman knew the arrangement could raise questions. During an August 2026 appearance on the Dallas Dialogue with Dale podcast, he said he had spoken with NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell about his Dolphins role.“I’ve talked to the commissioner, and he’s fine with what I’m doing and my role,” Aikman said during the podcast appearance.Aikman also argued that relationships naturally exist throughout NFL broadcasting. He pointed out that broadcasters build friendships with players and coaches across the league, even when they are covering those teams.There is another reason his situation should not create a major scheduling problem in 2026. The Dolphins are not on ESPN’s Monday Night Football schedule this season. Aikman addressed that point during the same Dallas Dialogue with Dale appearance, saying, “The Dolphins are not expected to be very good this year,” before explaining that Miami has no Monday night game this season.Still, the restrictions give Troy Aikman a new set of boundaries to follow. He can advise the Dolphins and remain one of ESPN’s leading NFL analysts, but he cannot have unrestricted access to teams while preparing for broadcasts.The NFL already created a framework for handling a broadcaster with a direct connection to an NFL team. Now, with Aikman working with Miami, the same framework applies to him.

Rodriguez’s engagement ring has previously been estimated at around £1.5 million, putting it among the most eye-catching celebrity rings in recent years. That choice could also make practical sense for the couple, particularly given the size of her engagement ring.The jeweller added that Rodriguez sometimes wears her engagement ring on the opposite hand because wearing both rings together may not be comfortable."It's also not unusual to see someone with an engagement ring this large wearing it on the opposite hand. Very large engagement rings don't always sit comfortably alongside a wedding band, so many brides choose to wear them separately depending on the occasion."Despite Ronaldo’s enormous wealth and the reported value of Rodriguez’s engagement ring, their wedding bands are estimated to be relatively modest by celebrity standards.Taylor put the likely price at between £1,000 and £2,500 per ring, or roughly $1,300 to $3,400 each. Patrick Mahomes is making progress in his recovery, but his latest appearance has reminded Kansas City Chiefs fans that the quarterback still has work to do before the 2026 NFL season. Mahomes watched the team’s preseason opener from the sidelines while wearing a large brace on his left knee. His determination remains strong, yet the sight has added another layer of uncertainty to his race to be ready for Week 1.The Chiefs kept Mahomes out of their preseason opener against the Los Angeles Rams as he continues recovering from the serious knee injuries that ended his 2025 campaign. The three-time Super Bowl champion tore both his ACL and LCL, creating a long rehabilitation process before he could return to football activities.Mahomes has since been cleared to practice and has taken part in limited work. He was also on the Arrowhead Stadium turf before Saturday’s game, going through pregame activity while still protecting his left knee with a substantial brace.That image naturally drew attention. Mahomes has built his reputation on extending plays, escaping pressure and making throws from difficult positions. Those movements demand confidence in his knee, especially once contact returns.Still, Mahomes has insisted that his recovery is moving in the right direction.“It feels great, pushing every single day, trying to stack days together,” Mahomes said last Sunday.He also acknowledged that the biggest challenge may be resisting the instinct to simply play through discomfort.“I feel like when you're tired, sometimes you don't even think about it. So, I'm trying to protect it, but at the same time, I’m trying to push it and get myself ready to go for the season.”For Kansas City, that balance could be crucial. The goal is not simply to get Mahomes back on the field. The Chiefs need their franchise quarterback healthy enough to withstand the demands of a full NFL season.Mahomes has made it clear that Week 1 remains the target, but neither he nor head coach Andy Reid wants to make a firm prediction this far ahead.“I’m optimistic, and I know he is," Chiefs coach Andy Reid said of Mahomes. "He’s extremely optimistic. But I think you’ve got to see how things go. Let’s just see where we’re at and not make any predictions or anything else. Take it day by day and see where it goes.”Kansas City has also added Justin Fields, giving the team another experienced option at quarterback if Mahomes needs additional recovery time. The move provides insurance without changing the Chiefs’ preferred plan, which remains centered on Mahomes.Mahomes understands that his rehabilitation will continue even after he returns to football activity. He described the challenge as learning to play with his current limitations while gradually rebuilding his confidence and strength.“I forget about it sometimes,” he said. “I try to be smart, as I said, but there are times when you get through camp, man, you're trying to compete, practices are long, and I mean, you want to win the rep.""So, there are times when I do forget about it and just play football, which is a good thing, and then I'll have to do that again whenever we get to the regular season. So, it's about learning how to play with what I’ve got, and I feel like I'm able to move and do the things that I can, and we're going to keep pushing it and see where I can get it to. So I can hopefully get that okay to go out there and play Week 1."For now, the message from Mahomes and the Chiefs is simple: progress matters more than preseason urgency. The brace may look concerning, but the real test will come as contact work increases and the quarterback moves closer to opening day.

NEW DELHI: Sri Lanka's last Test win against India came under Angelo Mathews in 2015 in Galle—the venue for the first Test starting on Saturday. He was a new captain thenWhile all the talk leading up to the series has been around spinners playing the key role, Mathews highlighted that playing rank turners can backfire on home teams."If I am not mistaken, India played on quite a few ranked turners against New Zealand and South Africa. Sometimes, it could backfire. We played on ranked turners against foreign teams and it has backfired for us as well. Because it's not easy as a batsman to play on ranked turners no matter how good you are," Mathews told TOI on Friday.Mathews has been a part of a Sri Lankan team which had heady battles with India, especially on their own turf. He believes a player like Rishabh Pant should be backed by the management as he too could have an impact like Virender Sehwag did in Sri Lanka."I remember when Ajanta Mendis was running through the Indian batting line-up, Sehwag was the one standing tall. He was so destructive and such a disruption. Pant is such a player," Mathews said."Pant takes the game on as soon as he walks into the crease. So, bowlers, watch out. A player like that needs backing. A guy like that who can take the game away within a few hours should be backed," he added.A big part of succeeding in Sri Lanka is to be measured against playing spin.One can't afford to go into his shell. "It's about being proactive. I think if you are sweeping, sweep well. If you are using your feet, use your feet well. So, it's all about using your feet and also knowing your options of how to score runs on those wickets is going to be crucial.Mathews also stressed on the importance of not just focusing on spinners in Sri Lanka. "It's definitely not wise to believe that cricket in Sri Lanka will be dictated only by spin," he said. "I wouldn't rule out the faster bowlers also because they are skillful. Guys like Asif Fernando and Vishwa Fernando have a bigger role to play as well, especially with the new ball," he added.Sri Lankan cricket saw a sharp drop in the number of Test matches they played after the stalwarts like Kumar Sangakkara and Mahela Jayawardene retired. For Mathews, it is a big reason behind Sri Lanka's inconsistent performances."I don't think poor performance or whatever has to do anything with that. It's just that it's disappointing that the so-called big teams or who is not wanting to play too many matches against Sri Lanka is quite disheartening. And I think ICC has a bigger role to play in this," Mathews opined."We have not been consistent throughout which can happen to any team. The more we play, the more we learn. We are playing Test matches one year apart. Sri Lanka Cricket can discuss with ICC and other boards as well and try to accommodate more Test cricket," he added.Watch Sri Lanka vs. India 1st Test Day 1 on August 15, 2026, from 10 AM IST live on Sony Sports Ten 1 SD & HD and Sony LIV.

Article Title: Meet Bianca Adler: The 18-year-old from Melbourne who turned back 400 metres from Everest’s summit, then returned a year later and made history
Article Text:
18-year-old Bianca Adler turns back 400m from Everest summit, returns a year later to make historyPhoto: Bianca Adler/ Instagram

A dream deferred

A year of preparation

The summit push

The descent begins

A proud family

A message to others

Not just Mount Everest

What’s next?

In the pre-dawn darkness of the world’s highest mountain, an 18-year-old from Melbourne stood on top of the world. Bianca Adler had just become the youngest Australian to summit Mount Everest , completing a feat that had eluded her just 12 months earlier, according to reports.At about 2:20am Nepal time, after an eight-hour climb from Camp 4 at 8,000 metres, Bianca reached the 8,849-metre summit alongside her guides, Pemba and Ngdu. A social media post just before 8am AEST announced the news to the world. But for Bianca and her family, the moment was about more than just a record; it was about resilience, determination and the courage to try again.Bianca’s journey to the summit began long before she set foot on Everest. Growing up in the French Alps, she developed a love for the mountains at a young age. By her teens, she was already setting records, becoming the youngest woman to summit both Manaslu (8,163m) and Ama Dablam (6,812m) at just 16, according to ABC News.But Everest was different. In May 2025, on her first attempt, Bianca made it to 8,450 metres — just 400 metres from the summit,before dangerous weather forced her to turn back.Strong winds posed a safety risk, and her hands and toes were going numb, the first sign of frostbite.“I couldn’t see anything; there was snow blowing everywhere,” she wrote on Instagram after making it back to safety. “It was an extremely tough decision, but I always want to choose life over a potential summit.”She made another attempt the following night but was overcome with exhaustion. Both she and her father, Paul, were diagnosed with high-altitude pulmonary oedema and dehydration during that expedition.Bianca did not give up. She spent the next year training, acclimatising and preparing for a second attempt. In April 2026, she and Paul returned to Nepal, spending a month acclimatising on different mountains and visiting Camp 2 before resting at Base Camp for a week, as per the report.They needed repairs to their climbing ropes and better weather before making a push towards the summit. That involved a 1am departure to go up through the icefall, rest at Camp 1, then continue onto Camp 2 where Paul remained.After two nights, Bianca continued on and began the final climb. She left Camp 4 around 6pm, climbing through the night in temperatures as low as -20 degrees.In a radio call with her father from the summit, Bianca said she felt “really good, but the weather is really bad”.“I feel really good up here actually, like physically I feel great,” she told Paul, who was waiting at Camp 2 in -20 degree conditions. “I spoke to her on the summit and she said she was very cold, it was windy but she felt OK, and they were going to take some pictures quickly and get out of there...It’s extremely dangerous up there and you feel very nervous for your life,” Paul said, according to ABC News.Bianca’s mother, Fiona, who was the third Australian woman to summit Everest, said the early summit time was a small price to pay for a safe and successful climb.“She is there well before the masses of people still on their way up...This is important for safety as it’s meant that she’s been able to climb at her pace and not get stuck and get cold in a long queue," Fiona said, as per the report.After reaching the summit, Bianca began her descent. By early morning, she had made it back to Camp 4, still in the “death zone” where there is not enough oxygen to sustain human life for an extended period.“I feel pretty awful, but I still have to go to Camp 2,” Bianca said in a short recording, struggling for breath. “I’m just resting, I’m just trying to take it one step at a time.”“It was so beautiful. Coming down was definitely a lot harder though. But, yes, it’s really tough.”Her dad said it would likely take her another day to reach Camp 2, where he was waiting. They will then descend together to Base Camp.Paul and Fiona were emotional and proud of their daughter’s achievement.“She was very determined and motivated to do this... We’re extremely proud of what she’s done; just having a goal and a dream and working for many years towards it. It’s a very proud moment for us," her father, Paul said, as per the report.Bianca takes the title of the youngest Australian to summit Mt Everest from Gabby Kanizay, who reached the top as a 19-year-old in 2022.Bianca has spoken about her motivation for mountain climbing. She often posts about it on her social media handles."Climbing for me isn’t just about the views on the summit, it’s about pushing myself and training towards a goal. I trained enough to feel good, and be able to appreciate being the highest person in the world, to point out mountains on the descent, and to have stayed safe the whole climb."I have dreamed of this moment ever since I first learnt about Everest, and I’m so happy everything went well. I am so grateful for all of the support by my friends, family and various communities 💓💓 I truly hope I can inspire more young people to do hard things, set big goals and work towards them!," she said in a social media post on May 21, 2026.Before climbing Mount Everest, Bianca Adler reached the summit of Mt Manaslu and created history by becoming the youngest woman in the world to summit this peak. Sharing the news, she had said in a social media post in 2025, "On the 25th of September, I reached the true summit of Mt Manaslu at 8163m! I did this with my amazing sherpa @jangbu.sherpa.374 as I became the youngest woman in the world to summit this peak."She further shared, "The highest I had been prior to this was touching 7000m and going above this was a massive step and I definitely relied on the oxygen a lot."Unfortunately at about 7900m, Dad got severe snow blindness and had to descend with his sherpa, as he couldn’t see at all. After we summited, Jangbu and I caught up to dad on the way down at about 7100m and descended with them."This was the hardest thing I have ever done and I am so glad all of my training has paid off."For Bianca, the adventure is not over yet. She still has to finish her final year of high school. “That’s going to be her next goal, is getting through year 12,” her father said, according to ABC News.But for now, she can rest on the knowledge that she has achieved something extraordinary. She turned back 400 metres from the summit, then returned a year later and made history.From turning back just 400 metres from Everest’s summit to returning a year later and making history, Bianca’s journey is a powerful reminder that sometimes the greatest victories begin with the courage to try again.
Article Summary: Bianca Adler, 18, is the youngest Australian to summit Mount Everest. On her first attempt in May 2025, Bianca turned back 400 metres from the summit. She spent the next year training, acclimatising and preparing for a second attempt. At about 2:20am Nepal time, after an eight-hour climb from Camp 4 at 8,000 metres, she reached the 8,849-metre summit.

Article Title: Super Bowl LXI lands on Valentine’s Day for the first time in history creating an unusual football-versus-romance showdown

Super Bowl LXI (Getty Images)

Super Bowl LXI and Valentine’s Day create a unique clash

Super Bowl 2027 brings another major change for NFL fans

Super Bowl LXI is about to create a very unusual sporting dilemma. The NFL ’s championship game is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valentine’s Day for the first time in Super Bowl history. With romance and football competing for the same Sunday, fans have already begun joking about dinner reservations, watch parties and the ultimate relationship compromise.The date alone is enough to make the 2027 Super Bowl stand out. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14, meaning couples will have to decide how they want to spend one of the biggest nights on the American sporting calendar.For football fans, the answer may seem obvious. For couples with different priorities, however, the evening could require some negotiation.Social media has already embraced the idea. One Reddit commenter joked about the pressure on restaurants, writing:"The Valentine's Day brunch reservations are going to be harder to get than a Super Bowl ticket."Another post took the joke even further, imagining the holiday as a test of romantic loyalty:"Super Bowl on Valentine's? Peak relationship apocalypse incoming—guys choosing touchdowns over touchy-feely dates. Ladies, demand a halftime proposal or it's single season next year."The humor works because the conflict is so easy to imagine. A romantic dinner could overlap with pregame coverage. A reservation might clash with kickoff.And anyone hosting a Super Bowl party could suddenly find themselves planning around Valentine's Day expectations.There is also a convenient escape route. The game falls on Presidents' Day weekend, giving many people the chance to turn the occasion into a longer celebration. Couples could celebrate Valentine's Day on Saturday, watch the Super Bowl on Sunday and use Monday to recover from the late night.The unusual date is not the only reason Super Bowl LXI will be significant. ESPN will broadcast the championship game for the first time in network history, with ABC also carrying the event. ESPN has already outlined extensive programming and storytelling designed to build anticipation well before the game itself.The timing also feeds into a broader conversation about the Super Bowl calendar. The NFL has long faced calls to make the Monday after the championship game a national holiday, particularly because fans already tend to treat Presidents' Day weekend as a natural extension of Super Bowl celebrations.Commissioner Roger Goodell has previously discussed how changes to the NFL schedule could eventually push the Super Bowl toward Presidents' Day weekend. In comments cited in the original report, he said:"I think if you went to 18 weeks regular season that would probably occur," Goodell said at the time. "It is possible somewhere in the calendar. Could happen before that just because of the calendar, the way it lays out.But I think 18 weeks would get you to that point, and I think it would be a really great move."For now, February 14, 2027 remains a one-of-a-kind collision between football and romance. The NFL has confirmed the date, and fans have plenty of time to decide whether Super Bowl Sunday will be a date-night disaster, a couples' tradition or simply the perfect excuse to order wings and watch football together.
Article Summary: Super Bowl LXI is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valentine's Day for the first time in Super Bowl history. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14. The NFL has long faced calls to make the Monday after the championship game a national holiday.

Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair are two of the biggest names in professional wrestling. But they have had very different experiences in terms of money. Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, WWE and the UFC, while Flair made his name over more than four decades in WCW and WWE.But there is a big gap, and public net-worth numbers are best seen as estimates, not audited financial statements. Lesnar’s contracts in the modern era, UFC purses and limited-appearance model allowed him to make individual paydays that were much larger than what was generally available to wrestlers during Flair’s peak years. Meanwhile, Flair continues to earn from his name, appearances, licensing and wrestling-related projects, despite the financial difficulties that have beset his wealth over the years.Brock Lesnar seems to be in a better financial state at the moment. Celebrity Net Worth estimates his net worth at $10 million, whereas NDTV reported an estimate of $17 million in June 2026. Other outlets have published higher numbers, a testament to the uncertainties that come with calculating celebrity net worth.Ric Flair is worth much less. His net worth has been estimated to be $500,000 by Celebrity Net Worth, but other estimates online have put the figure at a much higher number.The variation reflects the absence of publicly verified personal financial records, and the challenge of calculating assets, liabilities, royalties and ongoing income for a longtime entertainer.Lesnar’s wealth is intrinsically tied to his ability to command top dollar. He was an instant star in WWE after debuting in 2002, but he later moved away from the wrestling world to try his hand at the NFL and mixed martial arts before returning to WWE as an established crossover star.Lesnar’s career in WWE has been as much about scarcity as it has been about star power. He was often employed on a limited schedule around major storylines and premium live events for most of his later career instead of working weekly.Lesnar’s UFC career distinguished his money story from most WWE stars. After leaving professional wrestling, he came into MMA and immediately became a big draw. Beating Randy Couture for the heavyweight championship at UFC 91 made him a legit heavyweight champion and gave him a serious bump in commercial appeal.Lesnar has also earned money from endorsements and appearances. Jimmy John’s and other commercial deals are among his previous endorsement deals, and his celebrity status has helped his value outside the ring.He has also kept his lifestyle very private. Recent reports have pointed out that he prefers a rural lifestyle and owning vast amounts of land, rather than the high-profile celebrity lifestyle that many sports stars enjoy.Ric Flair’s financial story started in an era when the economics of professional wrestling were very different. The Nature Boy became one of the defining stars of the National Wrestling Alliance, World Championship Wrestling and WWE, headlining big events and winning championships through a career that spanned several decades.Flair made a ton of money in his time with WCW. One published estimate puts his WCW earnings from 1996-2000 at about $1.95 million. But the size of his earnings did not translate directly into lasting wealth because of taxes, legal obligations, medical expenses and other financial pressures.He also made a lot of money from his WWE career. Flair was a wrestler, manager and personality and stayed a close associate of the company for years. In 2005, during a divorce hearing, it was revealed that his annual WWE salary was reportedly around $500,000, showing how much he could make from wrestling even later in his career.Of the two stars, Flair's financial history is the starkest contrast. Celebrity Net Worth states that in 2000, the IRS filed a lien of more than $870,000 against him, and his further tax problems damaged his finances. The same source reports that in 2019 there was a major medical emergency that resulted in a medical bill of approximately $1.8 million.These pressures help explain why lifetime earnings and current net worth can look so dramatically different. Making millions in a career doesn’t always translate to keeping millions after taxes, debts, medical expenses and other costs.Lesnar’s future financial prospects will probably continue to be linked to his standing as a top-tier combat sports attraction. As his active wrestling career is changing, his name still has value for special appearances, merchandise, licensing and media projects.Flair’s earning model is a unique one. At 77, his money-making opportunities are increasingly linked to his legacy rather than regular ring competition. He still turns up at wrestling events, signs autographs and does other promotional stuff.Lesnar has a path to victory in the modern economics of sports and one of the rare WWE-to-UFC crossover careers. Flair’s financial legacy isn’t so much the wealth he has today, but the incredible value he brought to pro wrestling in terms of sales. Their careers demonstrate two different paths a wrestling superstar can take to earn money: Lesnar with premium modern contracts and crossover sports earnings, and Flair with longevity, character, championships and lasting brand recognition.
Article Summary: Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair are two of the biggest names in professional wrestling. But they have had very different experiences in terms of money. Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, WWE and the UFC. Flair made his name over more than four decades in WCW and WWE.

Article Title: “I just want to share that with all these little kids”: How Sophie Cunningham's $10,182 act of kindness turned WNBA frustration into a heartwarming moment for families in need
Article Text:
How Sophie Cunningham's $10,182 act of kindness turned WNBA frustration into a heartwarming moment for families in need(Getty)

Sophie Cunningham turned her WNBA fines joke into a $10,182 act of kindness

Sophie Cunninghum past Ronald McDonald House connection goes back to 2015

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sophie Cunningham had plenty of reasons to be frustrated in 2025. The Indiana Fever guard picked up multiple WNBA fines before a knee injury ended her season early. But a joke she made during that stretch took an unexpected turn. What started as a GoFundMe for fines or even a yacht raised $10,182. Cunningham then chose to give the money to a cause that had already touched her life.On Oct. 2, 2025, Sophie Cunningham launched a GoFundMe with a $26,000 goal. The Indiana Fever guard kept things playful when she explained the reason behind it.“This is more of a joke than anything. For fines only or to charity or for a yacht idk…,” Cunningham wrote on the GoFundMe page.The joke quickly caught on with her supporters. Over the next five days, 171 people donated to the fundraiser. Contributions ranged from $5 to $2,699, and the total eventually reached $10,182.That was when Cunningham decided the money would take a different path. “A yacht would be nice, but whatever we raise here will be going directly to Ronald McDonald House Charities. I’ll take care of my own fines. Y’all are the best,” Cunningham wrote in an update on the GoFundMe page, according to the Indianapolis Star's Oct.10, 2025 report.The decision came after a season in which Cunningham had become increasingly vocal about her frustrations with the WNBA. She had received multiple fines after speaking publicly about league officiating.In an August episode of her podcast, Show Me Something, Sophie Cunningham explained her disciplinary record with a joke of her own.“I’m officially 3-for-3 on being fined by the WNBA,” she said during the episode.She also explained why she continued to speak out, saying, “I promise you, everyone in our league feels that way and I’m just kind of the only one who says something.”So the fundraiser made sense at the moment. Sophie Cunningham had joked about the fines, fans responded and the money started coming in. Yet when she had more than $10,000 sitting in the fundraiser, she did not use it to erase the fines that had inspired the idea.Instead, she picked Ronald McDonald House Charities. That choice also came during a difficult personal stretch. Cunningham's 2025 season ended on Aug. 17 after she tore the MCL in her right knee. She later spent time on the sideline alongside several injured Fever teammates, including Caitlin Clark and Sydney Colson.During the Fever's exit interviews, Cunningham made it clear that she planned to return strong. When reporters asked whether she expected to be healthy for the 2026 season, she answered, “Hell yeah, man,” before saying she hoped to ramp up basketball activities in January.The fundraiser gave Cunningham a chance to do something positive while she waited for her own return.The charity was not just any random act. Sophie Cunningham first encountered Ronald McDonald House Charities as a teenager.Ronald McDonald House Charities helps families stay close to their children while they receive medical treatment. Its programmes provide places to stay, meals and other support for families facing difficult medical situations. Cunningham’s donation therefore went toward a cause that helps families during some of the hardest moments of their lives.On 2015, the Columbia Missourian reported on Cunningham's visit to a Ronald McDonald House in Chicago while she prepared for the McDonald's All-American Game. She met Brian and Jennifer Godish and their four-year-old son, Bradley, who had leukemia. Cunningham played with Bradley, built wooden train tracks with him and joined other children for basketball. She also volunteered to visit children who could not leave the hospital.“It makes me smile because this is how my parents raised me, and I’m just a little bit of who they are. I just want to share that with all these little kids and their parents,” Cunningham told the Columbia Missourian during that 2015 visit.Ten years later, she was once again giving to the same organisation. This time, her fans helped her raise the money.What began as a joke about WNBA fines ended with Sophie Cunningham choosing kindness over keeping the money for herself, adding a meaningful chapter to a connection that started long before her Indiana Fever career.
Article Summary: Sophie Cunningham started a GoFundMe page to raise money for fines or a yacht. The Indiana Fever guard then chose to give the money to Ronald McDonald House Charities. Cunningham first encountered the charity as a teenager during a McDonald's All-American Game.

Article Title: Can Nico Daws become the New Jersey Devils’ No. 1 goalie? Martin Brodeur believes he deserves the chance

Can Nico Daws beat Jake Allen and David Rittich for the Devils’ No. 1 goalie spot?

The New Jersey Devils will enter the 2026-27 season without a clear No. 1 goaltender, but Hall-of-Fame goalie Martin Brodeur believes Nico Daws deserves a real chance to take the job. After moving Jacob Markstrom to the Florida Panthers, New Jersey has left the door open for a new starter to emerge.Jake Allen and David Rittich are also in the mix, but Daws could have the biggest opportunity of his young NHL career. Brodeur, who serves as the Devils’ executive vice president of hockey operations, believes the 25-year-old deserves an opportunity to show what he can do in the NHL.According to Brodeur, the Devils are comfortable letting their goaltenders compete for the starting job rather than naming a clear No. 1 before the season begins. “The best starter is going to get the net,” Brodeur told The Hockey News. “I don't think there's a clear-cut No. 1 goalie in net.”That gives Daws a real opening. The 2020 third-round pick has spent much of his career moving between the NHL and AHL, and Brodeur believes the Devils have not given him enough chances to show what he can do.“Nico Daws is a kid who needs a chance,” Brodeur said. “We've been developing him for four years.We didn't put great teams in front of him in Utica and obviously his development slowed down because of that. But we need to give him a chance to see what we have.”While Daws has limited NHL experience, he has already delivered one performance that stands out. In the Stadium Series game against the Philadelphia Flyers at MetLife Stadium, he stopped 51 shots. Brodeur still remembers that performance when discussing Daws’ potential.“We put him into the Stadium Series game at MetLife Stadium in front of 70,000 people and he had 51 saves against the Flyers. He's got it, I really believe in him, we just never gave him a chance,” Brodeur said.That belief could be important for Daws as he competes with Allen and Rittich. Allen brings much more NHL experience, while Rittich has also spent years in the league. But neither has been locked into a heavy workload in recent seasons.Brodeur acknowledged that Markstrom will be missed but believes the current group can give New Jersey what it needs.“Jake showed us a lot last year when he had to play. He played some solid minutes for us,” Brodeur said. “We feel that both goalies are able to play.”If Daws can make the most of his opportunity, he could quickly move from an inexperienced option to the Devils’ top goalie. Brodeur has made his belief clear. Now Daws has the chance to prove it on the ice.

She had stepped away from tennis for more than a year and was also trying to understand what she wanted from her career and her life.For Osaka, self-care is not about putting herself before her daughter. It is about making sure she is in a good place so she can also be there for her child.In her conversations about motherhood and mental health, Osaka has spoken about setting boundaries, taking time for herself and paying attention to what she needs. That can mean taking a quiet moment, meditating, getting enough rest when possible or simply saying no when something feels like too much.Her message also pushes back against the idea that mothers must always put themselves last.Being a mother does not mean a woman has to ignore her own feelings, needs or identity.Osaka’s approach is simple. A mother can love her child deeply and still need time for herself. In fact, taking care of her own mental and emotional health can help her be more present for her child.Tennis had been a huge part of Osaka’s life for years. She became world No. 1 and won four Grand Slam singles titles, including the US Open in 2018 and the Australian Open in 2019, 2021 and 2022.But success also came with pressure. Osaka made headlines in 2021 when she withdrew from the French Open after explaining that media duties were affecting her mental health. She later stepped away from tennis for an extended period.Becoming a mother gave her another chance to look at her life from a different point of view.Osaka returned to professional tennis in January 2024 after giving birth. The comeback was not easy. She had to rebuild her body, return to the demands of professional sport and deal with the normal ups and downs of competition.But motherhood also helped her understand that tennis was only one part of who she was.Winning was still important to her, but it was no longer the only thing that defined her. She could be a tennis player, a mother and her own person at the same time.That change in thinking also helped Osaka become more open about her emotions. Instead of feeling that she always had to appear strong, she became more comfortable talking about difficult moments and asking for support.Osaka has spent much of her career in the public eye. Her matches, interviews and personal life have all received huge attention. That level of attention can be difficult for anyone, and motherhood has given her even more reason to protect her private life and mental space.She has spoken about how hard it once was for her to say no because she worried about disappointing people. Over time, she learned that she could not make everyone happy and did not have to accept every demand placed on her.That lesson became an important part of how she approaches motherhood.For Osaka, boundaries can mean choosing when to work, taking time away from social media, protecting family time or simply refusing to take on something that could leave her overwhelmed.These choices are not about shutting people out. They are about knowing when she needs to step back.Her experience also sends an important message to other mothers. Saying no does not mean you care less. Taking a break does not mean you are lazy. Asking someone for help does not mean you have failed.Sometimes, protecting your own peace is what allows you to give more of yourself to the people you love.Perhaps the biggest lesson from Osaka’s story is that mental health should not be treated as something people have to hide.She has spoken openly about anxiety, pressure and the challenges that came with being a top athlete. She has also talked about wanting her daughter to grow up in an environment where talking about feelings is normal.Osaka has encouraged the idea that children should be able to express themselves, ask for help and understand their emotions. She has also talked about simple habits such as meditation, quiet time and spending meaningful time with family.For her, these lessons are not only things she can tell her daughter. They are things she can show her through her own actions.When a mother rests when she needs to, she shows her child that rest is important. When she talks about her feelings, she shows that emotions are normal. When she asks for help, she teaches her child that nobody has to deal with everything alone.That may be one of the most important parts of Osaka’s message.Motherhood does not have to mean losing yourself. A woman can still have dreams, a career, friendships, personal goals and time for herself while being a loving and devoted mother.Osaka’s journey shows that self-care is not about choosing yourself instead of your child. It is about making sure you are also cared for.For the tennis star, that balance has become part of the mother she wants to be. Her words, “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter,” capture that idea in the simplest way. Taking care of yourself is not taking love away from your child. Sometimes, it is what helps you give that love with more patience, energy and presence.
Article Summary: Tennis star Naomi Osaka reveals how self-care changed her approach to parenting. Osaka became a mother in July 2023 when she welcomed her daughter, Shai. The four-time Grand Slam champion has been open about her struggles with anxiety and pressure.

Mojang is keeping the content pipeline flowing in Minecraft, and the excitement amongst the community is at an all-time high. It will bring a lot of things, including a brand new biome, a new wood set, furniture blocks, and a brand new structure to discover.Below we have all the details you need to know about the Minecraft Third Drop 2026.The Third Drop 2026 is an upcoming game drop that features dappled forests, abandoned camps, the poplar wood set, wool slabs and stairs, cushions, straw beds, and concrete slabs and stairs.Mojang is testing all the features through the snapshots, and players have already been able to experience most of them.The headline addition of the Third Drop is an entirely new overworld biome. The dappled forest consists of poplar trees with orange, yellow, and red leaves, as well as dirt blocks covered with leaf litter, new red shrubs, and brown mushrooms. After the Chaos Cubed drop took players deep underground, it is a breath of fresh air to have a brand-new destination to discover on the surface.The addition of poplar trees also brings a new wood set, which is a warm grey colour when broken down into planks and slabs. The poplar wood set comes in red, orange, and yellow leaf colors, and poplar saplings can be sold by wandering traders. It is a beautiful addition to the game's palette that builders in particular are going to go absolutely wild for.Scattered through the dappled forest are abandoned camps. They are small structures built from wool stairs and featuring chests or barrels to loot, with a tent-like visual design that fits the woodland explorer fantasy the biome is clearly going for. Having a lootable point of interest in a forest biome gives survival players an actual reason to push into unfamiliar territory.Even better, some abandoned camps contain maps hidden inside their chests. These maps lead to other abandoned camps or various other types of structures in the Overworld, making exploration feel genuinely rewarding in a way that few Minecraft updates have managed before.The drop also brings wool stairs, wool slabs, and wool cushions. Cushions in particular give players a genuine seat block, and pairing them with straw beds gives interiors a soft, homey layer that Minecraft's blocky palette has always struggled to deliver without workarounds.Straw beds are a new bed variant that lets players sleep through the night without changing their spawn point. They can only be used once and will be destroyed after use, and cannot be used in the Nether or the End.It is an elegant solution for players who want to skip the night on long expeditions without permanently shifting their respawn location.Concrete slabs and stairs have also been added as part of the final batch of features from the third drop, rounding out a building-focused update that is sure to keep the community's creative side busy for months to come.The Third Drop 2026 will certainly be pretty exciting to see when it arrives.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “She’s my everything. I love her” How Tom Brady’s mother Galynn defied cancer and stood by the star QB through adversity and his historic Super Bowl comeback
Article Text:
How Tom Brady’s mother Galynn defied cancer and stood by the star QB through adversity and his historic Super Bowl comeback(Getty)

How Galynn Brady ’s cancer diagnosis changed the family’s 2016 season

How Tom Brady supported his mother while facing his own adversity

How Galynn Brady fought through treatment with one goal in mind

How Super Bowl LI became Galynn Brady victory too

Why Robert Kraft gave Galynn Brady her own Super Bowl ring

How Galynn Brady recovery brought another reason for Tom Brady’s family to celebrate

How Galynn’s strength became part of Tom Brady’s story
